title: Geospatial foundation models and deep learning for climate resilience: a review of transfer, uncertainty and decision readiness
abstract: arXiv:2611.30198v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Geospatial foundation models can reuse information learned from large Earth-observation archives, but their value for climate resilience depends on whether that information transfers to unfamiliar events, regions and observing conditions. This review connects advances in deep learning with the evidence needed for hazard monitoring and early warning. A descriptive audit of 137 full-text hazard-application studies is interpreted alongside a separate corpus of 37 model and benchmark records. Ninety-eight application studies reported an out-of-distribution experiment, whereas headline evaluations included held-out events in 31 studies, regions in 25 and sensors in only two. None of the ten studies coded for geospatial foundation-model fine-tuning used sensor holdout as a headline test. translated_title: 地理空间基础模型与深度学习助力气候韧性：迁移、不确定性与决策就绪性综述
translated_abstract: 地理空间基础模型能够复用从大规模对地观测档案中学习到的信息，但它们对气候韧性的价值取决于这些信息能否迁移到陌生的事件、地区和观测条件中。本综述将深度学习的进展与灾害监测和预警所需的证据联系起来。本文对137篇灾害应用全文研究进行了描述性审计，并结合一个包含37条模型和基准记录的独立语料库加以解读。其中98项应用研究报告了分布外实验，而在核心评估中，31项研究设置了留出事件、25项设置了留出地区，仅有2项设置了留出传感器。在10项针对地理空间基础模型微调进行编码的研究中，没有一项将传感器留出作为核心测试。共有16项研究记录了与不确定性相关的方法，其中2项采用了经过明确校准的概率输出。这些相互重叠的统计结果描述了……
tldr: 本综述通过对137篇灾害应用研究与37条模型基准记录的系统审计发现，地理空间基础模型在气候韧性应用中的分布外评估（尤其是传感器迁移测试）和不确定性校准严重不足，距离真正支撑灾害监测与预警的决策就绪性仍有明显差距。
en_tdlr: This review of 137 hazard-application studies and 37 model/benchmark records finds that geospatial foundation models for climate resilience rarely undergo rigorous out-of-distribution evaluation—especially across sensors—or calibrated uncertainty quantification, limiting their decision readiness for hazard monitoring and early warning.
